record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; code and notebooks were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports an outcome from adding a refusal direction, but does not say it reproduces the original method or report an ablation result.
record.gate_note: The README describes ablation in the quickstart and lists abliteration-related material, but does not report an ablation or abliteration outcome. The reported steering outcomes are in the README's alpha paragraph.
record.test_reason: This is a safety-method library README, not a study. It uses the refusal direction as an inference-time steering tool (RefusalDirectionTrainer) and gives one anecdotal tuning note on a 0.5B model. That note has no baseline, no refusal rate, no ablation result and no capability metric, so it reports tool behaviour rather than testing whether the direction mediates refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The README says alpha 0.3 makes the 0.5B model refuse the lock-picking prompt while still answering the bread prompt. It also says 1.0 gives nonsense, 2.0 and up gives noise, and the default of 20 is far too strong. It concludes that the right alpha depends on the model.
record.recipe_differences: The README says the direction is extracted from contrast prompts and added at every layer, but does not specify the difference-in-means calculation or report the original ablation intervention. This is a library repository, not a stated replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering strength alpha changes the reported outcome: 0.3 retains an answer to the bread prompt, 1.0 produces nonsense on simple questions, and strengths from 2.0 produce noise.
record.problems: The README reports qualitative outcomes for one model and a small illustrative prompt set, with no baseline, quantitative refusal or capability metric, or uncertainty. The repository was not run or independently checked.
record.rows_left_out: No ablation or weight-edit results are reported in the README; the quickstart description and file names alone do not establish outcomes.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal on harmful prompts; induced refusal rate with a baseline; difference-in-means computation; quantitative capability retention.
Abliteration weight edit. Files exist (examples/demos/abliteration_and_defense.py, redteam/abliteration.py), but the README reports no outcome.
A single_direction_jailbreak case study is listed but not reported.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'challenges' and 'limits_scope' labels are dropped: the evidence is an untested library anecdote with no baseline. The README says the quickstart 'ablates it live', yet the code shown adds the direction at every layer, which is an internal inconsistency. Code and notebooks were not read.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report projecting the direction out, test the difference-in-means formula, or establish refusal removal by ablation. The addition example does not report a measured refusal rate or a baseline.

rows.locator: README, How it's organized, Steer alpha paragraph
rows.note: The README reports an answer rather than refusal for this benign prompt at the stated steering strength.
rows.check: Mislabelled as absent. V1 does not predict that a small addition makes benign prompts refused, so answering the bread prompt at alpha 0.3 is not evidence against V1. The paired result, that alpha 0.3 makes the model refuse the lock-picking prompt, is not recorded. There is no unsteered baseline, so the induced effect cannot be read.
